exposure: BMI category (underweight, normal weight, overweight, obese)
Singleton pregnancies conceived through IVF compared to those conceived naturally
cohort: All singleton pregnancies delivered at ≥ 22 weeks' in Slovenia between 2002 and 2015
finding: While pre-gravid overweight and obesity were associated with adverse perinatal outcomes in both IVF and non-IVF pregnancies, the study found a significantly lower impact of obesity on hypertensive disorders and cesarean delivery in IVF pregnancies, but a higher risk of neonatal mortality.
mod_finding: Pre-gravid obesity was associated with a higher rate of cesarean deliveries in both IVF and non-IVF pregnancies, with a lower effect size observed in the IVF group.
